purpose: Check whether freely available external files supply the missing daily Fed funds futures leg for the source-checked 6 November 2001 IEM pilot.

files.name: gss_data_aer_final.dta
files.coverage: Daily research data, 1990 onward in the supplied file; includes monetary-policy surprises and zero-to-fourteen-year forward rates.
files.reason: The event surprise and forward rates are derived research variables, not daily observations for a named Fed funds futures contract.

files.name: gss_program_aer_final.do
files.coverage: Published Stata transformations for the GSS data.
files.reason: The code multiplies mpspr by 100 to express the surprise in basis points; it does not reconstruct a daily Fed funds futures price path.

files.name: monetary-policy-surprises-data.xlsx
files.method: Thirty-minute changes around FOMC announcements in money-market futures covering the next four quarters.
files.reason: The workbook supplies announcement-window changes, not pre-announcement daily price levels. Its FF1 and FF2 observations are missing for this event.

files.name: sf_fed_monetary_policy_surprises.xlsx
files.reason: This is a second filename for the same workbook, not another independent data source.

files.name: lseg_fed_funds_contract_search.csv
files.reason: The file identifies a candidate contract but contains no historical observations.

files.name: fed_funds_december_2001_priceclose.csv
files.reason: The returned row has blank Date and Price Close fields.

contract_horizon_note.summary: Fed funds futures settle to the average daily effective federal funds rate for the delivery month. A deferred month can reflect more than one policy meeting; the December 2001 candidate also spans the 11 December meeting.
contract_horizon_note.implication: An exact contract-month mapping and horizon adjustment are required before interpreting a daily futures change as news solely about the 6 November meeting.

decision.report_role: Historical feasibility and external-validity agenda only; do not report the IEM-futures lead-lag estimates as reproduced evidence.
